h: Old Railways, Ponds and Pit Stops
p: The Family Cycle Trail is the route most first-timers head for. It loops around the forest for roughly ten miles, much of it on the beds of old railway lines that once carried coal and iron out of the Dean. That means gentle gradients and wide tracks, though there are a few longer drags, so take breaks. It links up with spots such as Beechenhurst, where you can stop for the Sculpture Trail or a play before pedalling back.

Just along the valley, Cannop Ponds are a peaceful place for a breather, with ducks, swans and the trees reflected in the water. They were created to power local industry back in the nineteenth century, a reminder that this green forest was once a busy working landscape full of mines and quarries.

Allow a half day for the family trail with stops, or longer if you're tackling the harder routes. Hose your bike down before you put it back on the car, as the mud here has a way of getting everywhere.
If you've got non-cyclists in the group, the Speech House, Clearwell Caves and Puzzlewood are all nearby to keep everyone happy.
